subject: Renewal pricing: term adjustment, seat rebalance & safety-net request
messages:
From: Jordan Price <procurement@lumenhealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal pricing request & term change

Markus —

Thanks for the call earlier. Quick follow-up from LumenHealth procurement. Our CFO has asked us to negotiate a 12‑month renewal (instead of the 24‑month term originally discussed) and to keep unit pricing flat for the first six months of the renewal while we complete an internal migration.

Concretely: can Redwood provide a short-term price hold for months 1–6, and a one-time credit (applied at invoice) to offset the churned seat delta during the migration? We have attached an updated PO draft.

We'd like to finalize terms by EOW so we can route for signatures.

Regards,
Jordan Price
Sr. Procurement Manager | LumenHealth
procurement@lumenhealth.com

Attachment: LumenHealth_PO_v2.pdf (attachment stub)
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <procurement@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing request & term change

Jordan — thanks for the clear ask and the PO. Appreciate the timeline.

Quick read: we can support a 12‑month renewal but need to balance the economics for Redwood and the operational overhead of a short initial term. Proposed compromise:

- Price hold: maintain current per‑unit rates for months 1–6 (no price change).
- Credit: one‑time migration credit equal to 10% of the first invoice after go‑live (to offset seat churn), applied as a bill credit.
- Commit adjustment: convert to a 12‑month commit with an option to extend to 24 months at a pre‑agreed uplift (3% discount cliff if extended within month 9).
- Safety-net: include a burst allowance (20% over committed capacity) for months 1–3 at no additional charge to handle migration spikes; excess above that billed at standard overage rates.

This preserves short‑term flexibility for LumenHealth while protecting our unit economics. If that sounds workable I can have a redline to the term sheet and pricing workbook to you by Wed.

Looping in Marissa for approval on the credit and David for finance/PO intake.

Thanks —
Markus Klein
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
Office: (415) 555‑0198

Attachment: proposed_pricing_sheet_v3.xlsx (attachment stub)
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@lumenhealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Jordan Price <procurement@lumenhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing request & term change

Markus — Jordan flagged this to me. The framework looks reasonable but our legal team has two asks: (1) an SLA credit trigger if sustained latency >150ms for more than 48h across production, and (2) a defined data retention clause for logs during the 12‑month term.

Also, the CFO would prefer the migration credit to be applied pro rata across the first two invoices instead of a single invoice credit.

Can you confirm whether the burst allowance can be scoped to regional (US‑west) capacity only — we want to avoid cross‑region failover affecting our billing.

Thanks —
Elena Soto
Director, Cloud Ops | LumenHealth
elena.soto@lumenhealth.com

Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing request & term change

Elena / Jordan —

Thanks — good, practical feedback. Quick responses inline and next steps below.

- SLA credit: we can add a latency SLA with a credit ladder. I’ll propose language: 5% invoice credit for a single 48h window breach (latency >150ms), escalating to 15% if repeated within 30 days. Exact wording in redline.
- Data retention: will include a 90‑day operational logs retention clause for the renewal term, with options to extend via addendum.
- Migration credit: we are OK with splitting the credit across the first two invoices (50% / 50%).
- Burst allowance: can be scoped to the US‑west pool only; cross‑region routing will be explicitly excluded from the burst allowance.

Action items:
1) I’ll upload a redlined term sheet (redline_term_sheet_2027-06-16.pdf) and updated pricing sheet to DocuSign for signature by Monday.
2) Marissa — can you confirm approval for a one‑time migration credit capped at 10% and the SLA credit ladder?
3) David — can you confirm that finance is comfortable with invoice credit flow (50/50 split) and how that maps to our billing system?

If internal signoff is good, Jordan — we should be able to send a DocuSign packet and PO acceptance link by EOD Monday so LumenHealth can route.

Best,
Markus

---
Markus Klein
